cards.title: Steady-State and Sparse Sampling Assumptions in Phoenix NCA
cards.claim: Phoenix NCA models 200-202 (plasma/blood) support both single-dose and steady-state data. For steady-state, the computation assumes equal dosing intervals (Tau) for each profile and that data is from a 'final' dose at steady state. Models 210-212 (urine) assume single-dose data. The engine supports rich datasets and sparsely-sampled studies (e.g., toxicokinetics).
conditions: When analyzing steady-state data, Tau must be provided and assumed constant across profiles.
When analyzing sparse data, the engine's sparse sampling algorithms are applied.
Urine models (210-212) are restricted to single-dose assumptions.
limitations: Assumes equal dosing intervals for steady-state; does not explicitly describe handling of unequal intervals in this excerpt.
Does not detail the specific algorithm for sparse sampling (e.g., L-FOCE vs. other methods).
cards.downstream_use: Informs data preparation steps (e.g., ensuring Tau is defined for steady-state studies). Clarifies that urine analysis is limited to single-dose contexts in this software version.
